Paper_name: The roles of the LpSTS and DLPFC in self-prioritization: A transcranial magnetic stimulation study
Summary: This study investigates the causal roles of the left posterior superior temporal sulcus (LpSTS) and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) within the Self-Attention Network (SAN) framework for self-prioritization. Using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to disrupt these regions in separate participant groups, the researchers examined performance on a self-matching task. Results showed that inhibiting the LpSTS reduced performance on self-related stimuli, establishing its causal role. Findings for the DLPFC were more complex, differing between analysis methods. The study provides direct evidence supporting the SAN model and clarifies the differentiated functions of its key nodes.
Author: Qiongdan Liang, Bozhen Zhang, Sinan Fu, Jie Sui, Fei Wang
Conclusion: The study established a causal role for the LpSTS in self-related processing, as its inhibition reduced performance on self-matching tasks, providing direct evidence for the SAN framework. The role of the DLPFC was less clear, with results varying between analysis methods. The findings advance the understanding of how different nodes within the SAN differentially contribute to self-prioritization in information processing.
